--- PART 1/5 ---

RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Parent fitness 269.88. Average per match over 100 rounds max 500. Against 11 opponents, average maybe 270 means avg 2.7 per round. Need improve."
STRATEGY: Parent is TFT-two-tats + always defect against confirmed defector, endgame defect, occasional defection if both D. Simulated the 12 population opponents and all-C baseline. Changed toward adaptive cooperation, retaliation, exploiter detection, pattern matching, and endgame defection.

--- PART 2/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "So an improved strategy could score around 290+ against most, except slot6." and "So we can aim for ~295."
STRATEGY: The parent cooperates by default, retaliates against defection, and defects in the endgame. The trace simulates the given probe strategies (one_D_TFT, four_D_TFT, four_D_ALLC, sustained_D, periodic_D) and other population slots to estimate scores. It proposes changes: detect exploiters via early defection rates, switch to periodic defection to keep a D in the last 10 rounds, and defect only on the final round against retaliatory opponents.

--- PART 3/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Given the complexity, maybe we can design a strategy that is generally good and then fine-tune. The parent strategy scored 269.88. All C scored ~279."
STRATEGY: The parent cooperates by default, retaliates against confirmed defectors, defects in the endgame, and occasionally defects when both sides defect. The trace simulates the parent against the listed probe strategies (one_D_TFT, four_D_TFT, four_D_ALLC, sustained_D, periodic_D) and considers changes such as periodic D against exploiters, earlier detection, and endgame defection timing.

--- PART 4/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "This is significantly better than parent's 269.88 and all C's 279. So this strategy should be a good improvement."
STRATEGY: The parent cooperates by default, retaliates against recent defections, defects in the endgame, and uses an exploiter mode with periodic defection against high-defection opponents. The trace simulates this revised strategy against the twelve listed opponents, including slot0, slot2, slot5, slot6, and slot10, and changes the exploiter-mode gap from 11 to 10, adds a one-time test for always-cooperating opponents at round 20, and refines endgame retaliation.

--- PART 5/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Let's test against a hypothetical opponent that defects every 3 rounds (rate 0.33). Our strategy enters exploiter mode at n=10."
STRATEGY: The parent cooperates early, then switches to always-defect against high-defection opponents, periodic defection against exploiters, and a round-20 test for non-retaliatory opponents. The trace simulates the revised strategy against TFT, always-C, slot0, slot2, slot5, slot6, slot10, and slot3. It changes the parent by removing the old defection condition and adding the round-20 test plus a round-22 always-defect trigger.
